ai.description: Cnemaspis amba reaches 35 mm SVL. It is brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Distinctive features include a keeled venter and a lack of precloacal pores.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis amba* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its throat, which is absent in most other sympatric dwarf geckos.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis amba* inhabits moist deciduous forests in the Northern Western Ghats, typically found on rock boulders and tree trunks at elevations around 600–800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Amba dwarf gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging from rock crevices at night to actively forage for small invertebrates on vertical surfaces.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis amba* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis amba* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
